orders.reason: Fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance with uncontrolled hypertension

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, can't keep up on his walks.

HPI: Over the past few months he has felt worn out, and the morning walk he used to do without thinking now takes more out of him; he has cut it short several times. Sleeping OK. No chest pain or pressure, no breathlessness at rest, no orthopnea, no ankle swelling, no palpitations, no lightheadedness. Appetite fine, weight steady. Mood good, no loss of interest. Has not been checking home BP since the fall.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, ASA 81.

Exam: BP 158/94 (repeat similar). Pulse regular. Looks well. No JVD. Heart regular, I may hear an extra sound at the apex but not sure. Lungs clear. No edema. Thyroid normal size.

A/P:
1. Fatigue / reduced exercise tolerance in a 66 yo diabetic with long-standing uncontrolled BP. Checking BMP, CBC, TSH, A1c today. Referring to cardiology for evaluation.
2. HTN - clearly above goal today and not monitoring. Restart home log.
3. T2DM - A1c today.

Reviewed when to go to the ED (chest pain, fainting, shortness of breath at rest). RTC after cardiology.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Clark - your blood count, thyroid, kidney function and electrolytes are all normal, so none of those explain the tiredness. A1c is 7.6, about where it has been. Cardiology should call you this week to set up the appointment; let us know if you don't hear from them.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks Doc. They called already, I go March 18.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix #2 IM L deltoid. Series complete. No reaction during observation.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Normal axis. PR and QRS intervals normal. Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No acute ST elevation. No Q waves.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm. Left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage criteria.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 03/18/2019
Re: Carl Clark, DOB 09/28/1952
Referred by: primary care

Dear colleague,

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Clark, a 66-year-old retired letter carrier, for several months of tiredness and a falling-off in how far and how fast he can walk.

He has diabetes and hypertension, the latter never well controlled by his account, along with hyperlipidemia. He takes lisinopril, metformin and amlodipine, plus aspirin 81 mg. No known drug allergies. Never smoker, no alcohol. His father had colon cancer at 70 and is deceased; his mother had diabetes and high blood pressure. Surgical history is a tonsillectomy in childhood and a knee arthroscopy at 55.

Exam: BP 160/96. Pulse 72 and regular. The apical impulse is displaced laterally and there is an S4. I hear no murmur. JVP is not raised, the lungs are clear and there is no peripheral edema; no evidence of heart failure.

Recent labs from your office show normal renal function and electrolytes.

ECG today: sinus rhythm, 72, with voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy.

Impression: Left ventricular hypertrophy, almost certainly the product of years of inadequately treated hypertension. I suspect the pressure load explains much of his reduced exercise tolerance.

Recommendations:
1. Transthoracic echocardiogram to characterize the hypertrophy and LV function; scheduled for 03/28.
2. Tighter BP control is the priority. I would increase amlodipine to 10 mg daily and aim for under 130/80. I will leave the adjustment with you.
3. Continue aspirin.

We would be glad to see him again as needed.

Cardiology
Allergies: NKDA

reports.text:
Complete 2D, M-mode and Doppler study. Technically adequate.
Left ventricle: normal cavity size. Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy; interventricular septum 1.3 cm and posterior wall 1.3 cm in diastole. Normal wall motion. LVEF 60% (biplane).
Right ventricle: normal size and function.
Atria: normal size.
Valves: aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation.
Aorta: normal root dimension.
Pericardium: no effusion.
IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with normal LV size and systolic function, LVEF 60%. Normal valves. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Call to patient re cardiology and echo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cardiology letter and echo report received and reviewed. Echo shows thickened heart muscle from his blood pressure with normal pumping function and normal valves.

Called pt. Explained the findings. Agreed to increase amlodipine 5 -> 10 mg daily per cardiology. New Rx sent to mail order, told him he can take two of the 5s until it arrives. Check home BP a few times a week; nurse BP check / visit in about 6 weeks. Ankle swelling can happen at the higher dose, call if it bothers him. He verbalized understanding.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP f/u on amlodipine 10.

Home log 126-138 / 76-84 over the past 4 weeks. Feels like his energy is coming back; walked the full loop twice last week. No ankle swelling. No dizziness.

BP much better today. Heart RRR, S4 still audible at apex. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: HTN with LVH - better controlled on lisinopril 20 + amlodipine 10. Continue. BMP today. Fatigue improving as pressure has come down. Recheck at the fall physical.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination Report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry - Annual Diabetic Eye Exam
Exam date 06/18/2019. Carl Clark, DOB 09/28/1952.
Best corrected acuity 20/25 OU. Pupils normal. Dilated exam: retina flat, no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization OU. Discs healthy.
Assessment: no diabetic retinopathy.
Plan: return in one year.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare AWV.

Interval: echo in March showed LVH, normal EF. Amlodipine to 10 in April; home BP mostly low 130s since. Energy back to baseline. Walking daily again.

Functional: independent, no falls, drives. Memory screen normal (3-word recall 3/3). Hearing and vision adequate. Lives with wife.
PHQ-2 0.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, ASA 81.

Exam: Vitals reviewed. Heart regular with S4, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: intact sensation, pulses palpable, skin fine.

Prevention:
- Colonoscopy: recommended once again; we talked about his dad. He says maybe next year. FIT offered as an alternative; declined for now.
- Flu shot at nurse visit in 2 weeks.
- Vaccines otherwise up to date (PCV13, PPSV23, Shingrix x2).

Labs: A1c, CMP, lipid, urine microalbumin.

RTC 6 months for diabetes.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs look stable: A1c 7.5, kidney and liver tests normal, urine protein normal, cholesterol similar to prior years. No changes needed now. Flu shot visit is on the 8th.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine given IM R deltoid. No complaints today. Tolerated well.

documents.title: Mail-order refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy requesting renewal of amlodipine 10 mg #90 and metformin 1000 mg #180. Last visit 9/2019, labs current. Sent per refill protocol, PCP cosigned.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, in-person appointment cancelled during the shutdown. Patient at home with his wife helping with the tablet. Identity verified.

Doing fine, staying home, walking around the block. Home BPs this month 128-136 / 76-82. Fasting fingersticks 130s-150s. Taking all meds; mail order delivering fine. No chest pain, dyspnea, swelling.

A/P: HTN controlled at home on current regimen. T2DM - no A1c today; will draw when the lab reopens to routine visits, likely summer. Continue metformin. Call with any problems.

Time 20 min.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination Report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry report. Exam 06/23/2020 (masked visit). Carl Clark.
Acuity 20/25 both eyes with glasses. Dilated fundus: no diabetic retinopathy, maculae clear OU.
Impression: diabetes mellitus type 2 without retinopathy. Recall 12 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit since the winter. Masked.

Snacking more being home all spring, but back to walking. No symptoms. Meds unchanged.

BP fine today. RRR, S4. Lungs clear. Feet: normal monofilament, no calluses or wounds, pulses palpable.

A1c 7.7, up a little. Talked about evening snacks and portion size; he'd like to try on his own before any added medication. Continue metformin 1000 BID.
BMP drawn.

RTC for AWV in September.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent.

Hanging in through the pandemic. Wife well. Walking. No falls, independent in ADLs/IADLs. Sleep fine. Mood good; PHQ-2 negative.

Meds reconciled, unchanged: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, aspirin 81.

Exam: normal vitals for him. Heart regular, S4 at apex, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet normal.

Preventive:
- Colon cancer screening again recommended; declines colonoscopy this year with COVID around; would "maybe do the mail kit." Will send FIT in the spring when he's ready - he asked to wait.
- Tdap - no tetanus booster on record in the last 10 years; give with flu shot next visit.
- Flu shot nurse visit 10/6.

Labs today. RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Clark, results from Tuesday: A1c 7.5, kidney function normal, urine microalbumin normal, cholesterol unchanged. Nothing new to do. Remember to bring your BP log next time.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: COVID screening questions negative at door. Fluzone HD L deltoid, Boostrix R deltoid. Tolerated without issue.

documents.title: covid shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My wife and I want the covid shot when we can get it. Do we sign up with you or somewhere else? With my sugar am I in an early group?

documents.title: RE: covid shot
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Mr. Clark, the state is running the first rounds through mass vaccination sites and pharmacies. People 65 and over are expected in the next phase, probably early in the new year. We will post sign-up instructions on the portal as soon as we have them. Yes, your age and diabetes both count.
